Re: LD 1711 - Resolve, to Allow Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Benefits to Be Used to Purchase Ready-to-cook Meals
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services, thank you for the opportunity to provide information neither for nor against LD 1711, Resolve, to Allow Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Benefits to Be Used to Purchase Ready-to-cook Meals.
This resolve would require the Department to request a waiver from the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) to allow ready-to-cook meals to be purchased with Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits and notify retailers and other providers of the rule change.
Currently (and without any waiver from FNS), SNAP recipients may purchase ready-to-cook meals. SNAP recipients may not, however, use SNAP benefits to purchase hot prepared foods. For the purposes of SNAP administration, 7 U.S.C � 2012(k), defines food as: "any food or food product for home consumption except alcoholic beverages, tobacco, hot foods or hot food products ready for immediate consumption." Most waivers for purchasing hot foods are associated with disasters where access to cooking facilities may be limited and are for a short duration of time. If there are specific foods or retailers that the sponsor has in mind, we would be happy to assist and explore options. As is currently written, the Department believes that this bill is unnecessary.
Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your deliberation of this bill.
Sincerely,

Ian Yaffe Director Office for Family Independence Maine Department of Health and Human Services

MEJ Testimony Neither For Nor Against LD 1711, Resolve, to Allow Supplemental
Nutrition Assistance Program Benefits to Be Used to Purchase Ready-to-cook Meals
April 2s, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Health and Human Sen/ices Committee. My name is Kathy Kilrain del Rio, I use she/her pronouns, and I'm
the Advocacy and Programs Director for Maine Equal Justice, a nonprofit legal aid provider working to increase economic security, opportunity, and equity for people in Maine. Our organization has decades of experience working with people with low incomes to support access to health care, food security, housing security, education and training programs, and other programs that support individuals and families in moving toward financial security so they can thrive. l'm testifying Neither For Nor Against LD 1711.
As you know, the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) helps families and individuals struggling with low incomes to meet their nutritional needs by providing food
assistance. It is one of the most successful anti-poverty tools we have available to us. Food essential to life. The flexibility provided by the SNAP program allows people to choose the foods they most need and to seek alternatives when there are shortages or the costs of certain
products becomes too high for their budgets.
We are testifying NFNA LD 1711 because we believe SNAP participants are already able to
purchase ready-to-cook foods that are cold from any retailer that is a SNAP vendor. However, one gap in accessing foods can be the inability to purchase hot foods with SNAP benefits. In
many stores, there are reasonably priced prepared foods that would make it easier for families
to quickly get a meal on the table. For example, by purchasing a heated rotisserie chicken, hot
meatballs, hot soup, or a hot pizza. These are commonly available at many grocery stores or
small "mom & pop" stores in many towns and cities across our state. These products can be
especially helpful for those individuals and families making do without electricity or living
somewhere without a stove or microwave - such as a motel or tent, which isn't uncommon for
people with very low incomes. There's a helpful overview of what is allowed and not allowed to
be purchased on the USDA's website as well as links to resources describing these for retailers:
https://www.fns.usda.qov/snap/eliqible-food-
items#:~:text=Households%2OCANNOT%20use%2OSNAP%20benefits%20to%20buv%3A&text =Vitamins%2C%2Omedicines%2C%2Oand%2Osugplements.,%2Dup%2Ofrom%20the%20store)
For this reason, we would recommend amending the bill to direct DHHS to explore any options
available to expand access to hot foods through a waiver or other process that could become
available.
Thank you for the opportunity to testify on this bill. l'm happy to try to answer any of your
questions.
